}}'''Ezio Rizzardo''' {{postnominals|country=AUS|AC|FAA|FTSE|FRS}} (born 26 December 1943 in [[Pederobba]], [[Italy]]) is a polymer chemist at the Australian research agency [[CSIRO]].<ref name="CSIRO">{{cite web | title=Dr Ezio Rizzardo | website=CSIRO | url=https://people.csiro.au/R/E/Ezio-Rizzardo | access-date=16 October 2018 | archive-date=12 August 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812114815/https://people.csiro.au/R/E/Ezio-Rizzardo | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in Italy, Rizzardo's family immigrated to Australia in 1957. After graduating from the [[University of New South Wales]], he studied the photochemistry of organic nitro compounds at the [[University of Sydney]], receiving his PhD in organic chemistry in 1969. He has worked on polymer chemistry at CSIRO since 1976.<ref name="CSIRO"/>

==Research==
His research interests include the kinetics and mechanisms of radical polymerization, and their commercial application.<ref name="CSIROpedia"/> Rizzardo is an acknowledged expert in chemical methods to control the polymer architecture produced by free radical polymerization.<ref name="AAS"/> His innovations include two techniques for polymer synthesis, [[nitroxide-mediated radical polymerization]] (NMP) and [[reversible addition−fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization]] (RAFT).<ref name="CSIROpedia"/> He is named as co-inventor on more than 40 patents.<ref name="CSIRO"/>

==Awards and honours==
Rizzardo has received multiple awards from CSIRO and the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] for his achievements, as well as the [[Centenary Medal]] (2003) and the [[Prime Minister's Prizes for Science#Prime Minister's Prize for Science|Prime Minister's Prize for Science]] (2011).<ref name="CSIROpedia"/>

In 2014, research by Thomson Reuters for their [[Clarivate Citation Laureates|citation laureate prize]] named Rizzardo as one of three CSIRO scientists who were likely contenders for the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]], citing their work on RAFT. Rizzardo quipped that he would not be holding his breath on the night the prizes were announced.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bridie Smith |url=http://www.smh.com.au/technology/sci-tech/csiro-scientists-graeme-moad-san-thang-and-ezio-rizzardo-named-as-nobel-prize-contenders-20140925-10lsai.html |title=CSIRO scientists Graeme Moad, San Thang and Ezio Rizzardo named as Nobel prize contenders |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=25 September 2014 |access-date=2014-09-25}}</ref> The trio had been awarded the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering#Clunies-Ross Award|ATSE Clunies-Ross Award]] earlier in the year.<ref name="ATSE">{{cite web | title=Clunies Ross Awards Previous Recipients | website=Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering (ATSE) | url=https://www.atse.org.au/atse/content/about/previous-recipients.aspx | access-date=16 October 2018 | archive-date=16 October 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181016130056/https://www.atse.org.au/atse/content/about/previous-recipients.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref>

He is a fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering|Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] (1994),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Ezio Rizzardo |url=https://www.atse.org.au/who-we-are/our-fellows/all-fellows/ezio-rizzardo/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Australian Academy of Technological Sciences & Engineering |language=en}}</ref> the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (2002)<ref name="AAS">{{cite web | title=Dr Ezio Rizzardo | website=Australian Academy of Science | url=https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/dr-ezio-rizzardo | access-date=16 October 2018 | archive-date=23 July 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723072202/https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/dr-ezio-rizzardo | url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Royal Society]] (2010).<ref name="RS">{{cite web | title=Ezio Rizzardo | website=Royal Society | date=19 September 2015 | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ezio-rizzardo-12180/ | access-date=16 October 2018}}</ref> He was appointed [[Companion of the Order of Australia]] in 2018.<ref name="CSIROpedia">{{cite web | title=Ezio Rizzardo | website=CSIROpedia | date=13 January 2015 | url=https://csiropedia.csiro.au/rizzardo-ezio/ | access-date=16 October 2018}}</ref>
